input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 imposes Singapore law with exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — Vendor-side territory outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and walk-away on its face. It also directly contradicts Section 28.2, which already grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County with only a customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out (that carve-out does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum). The shortest complete cure is to change the governing law in 28.1 to New York and delete the conflicting Singapore jurisdiction wording, leaving 28.2's venue intact so the clause sits at the preferred position.

ops.oldText: Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
ops.newText: the laws of the State of New York.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replace Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction in 28.1 with New York law, which is our preferred governing law and removes the direct conflict with the exclusive New York County venue already agreed in 28.2. Delaware, California, or England and Wales (with London courts) would be acceptable fallbacks.
proposal.summary: Change governing law in 28.1 from Singapore to New York and delete the conflicting Singapore exclusive jurisdiction wording.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
mappings.quote: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.
